title: Towards Controllable Hybrid Fairness in Graph Neural Networks

problem.claim: GNNs can exhibit fairness issues, including prejudicial predictions across sensitive attributes and substantially different prediction performance across node degrees.

gap.claim: Existing studies mainly address one fairness issue at a time, leaving models potentially unfair when multiple fairness issues occur simultaneously.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNNs are capable of mining graph-structured data.
Conventional GNNs can produce unfair outcomes across sensitive attributes and node degrees.
Prior work generally focuses on a single fairness issue despite the possibility of simultaneous fairness problems.

source_observation.claim: A model may face multiple fairness issues simultaneously.

interpretation.claim: Fairness assessment should consider multiple relevant dimensions rather than assuming that one addressed issue represents overall fairness.

application.claim: When evaluating graph models, examine fairness across both sensitive attributes and structural characteristics such as node degree.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish which fairness dimensions are relevant in every application.

unknowns: No method or technical approach is described.
No experiments, datasets, metrics, numerical results, or comparisons are provided.
No explicit author claim of novelty is provided.
